title: LabWriteBackRequest

AbnormalFlag.description:
What a result is, relative to its reference range.

Five members, not four, because `indeterminate` is a real answer — see
the module docstring on censored values. `openemr_abnormal_code()` maps
the four decidable ones onto OpenEMR's `proc_res_abnormal` list
(`no | yes | high | low`, spike §9) and refuses to map the fifth,
because there is no column value that means "we could not tell" and
writing `no` would be a lie with a patient in it.
AbnormalFlag.title: AbnormalFlag

BBox.description:
A rectangle on a page, in PDF points.

Coordinate convention, matching the doc-factory's recorded convention
exactly (`agent/evals/w2/factory/groundtruth.py` COORDINATE_CONVENTION)
so that ground truth and extractor output are directly comparable:
origin top-left, y increasing downward — PyMuPDF page space, on the
original clean layout rather than on a degraded scan.

`x1 >= x0` and `y1 >= y0`, not `>`: a zero-width box is real data. The
factory emits one for every unflagged lab result (an empty flag column
renders as `[306.0, 256.398, 306.0, 268.24]`), and rejecting it would
make the contract unable to describe a normal lab row.

page.description: 1-based page number within the source document.
page.title: Page

x0.description: Left edge, PDF points from the page's left edge.
x0.title: X0

y0.description: Top edge, PDF points from the page's top edge (y down).
y0.title: Y0

BBox.title: BBox

Comparator.description:
The censoring a lab report prints in front of a number. Values match
FHIR's `Quantity.comparator` value set, because a written-back result
surfaces as `Observation.valueQuantity` (D1, spike §5).
Comparator.title: Comparator

DocumentKind.description:
The two document kinds Week 2 extracts. Closed, because the supervisor
routes on it and the write-back path accepts exactly one of them: D2
forbids intake data reaching the chart, and the type is where that is
enforced (`LabWriteBackRequest` takes LAB_PDF and nothing else).
DocumentKind.title: DocumentKind

LabWriteBackResult.description:
One lab value to write, with everything the four-table insert needs and
everything the ledger needs to trace it back to a page.

`test_code` and `test_name` are both required because the spike found
`procedure_result.result_code` and `result_text` are both required or
"the code is dropped and replaced with a null-flavor" (§9).

`abnormal` may not be `indeterminate`: `openemr_abnormal_code()` refuses
to map it, because `procedure_result.abnormal` has no value meaning "we
could not tell" and writing `no` would put a false normal in a chart.

reported_at.description: -> procedure_report.date_report, which becomes both `effectiveDateTime` and `meta.lastUpdated` on the Observation (spike §9).
reported_at.title: Reported At

page.description: Page of the source document this value came from.
page.title: Page

bbox.description: Where on that page — D2's provenance requirement.

idempotency_key.description: D1's UNIQUE key. Required, with no default: invariant 6 has no exceptions, and a default would be one.
idempotency_key.title: Idempotency Key

LabWriteBackResult.title: LabWriteBackResult

comparator.description: None for an exact reading; set for a censored one such as `<5`.

QualitativeLabValue.description: A term rather than a number: `positive`, `not detected`, `trace`.
QualitativeLabValue.title: QualitativeLabValue

ReferenceRange.description:
The interval a result is judged against.

`low`/`high` are the machine-comparable form; `text` is what the report
actually printed, kept verbatim because it is what a citation quotes and
because plenty of ranges (`Negative`, `See note`) have no numeric form
at all. At least one of the three is required — an all-None reference
range is an extraction bug wearing a valid object's clothes.

text.description: The range exactly as printed, e.g. `70 - 99` or `Negative`.
text.title: Text

unit.description: The unit the bounds are in.
unit.title: Unit

ReferenceRange.title: ReferenceRange

WriteBackDocument.description:
The document half of the request.

Exactly one of `content_base64` and `existing_document_id`: a first
attempt sends the bytes, a retry after a partial failure names the
document OpenEMR already stored. `sha3_512` is required either way — it
is the document idempotency key and the first component of every
result's key, so a request without it could not be made idempotent at
all (invariant 6).

mime_type.description: Check by content before sending: a type outside OpenEMR's `files_white_list` is rejected as an empty 404 with no error (spike §10.6).
mime_type.title: Mime Type

content_base64.description: The file, base64-encoded. Omit when retrying against an id.
content_base64.title: Content Base64

existing_document_id.description: `documents.id` of a file already stored for this patient.
existing_document_id.title: Existing Document Id

category_path.description: OpenEMR document category the file is filed under.
category_path.title: Category Path

WriteBackDocument.title: WriteBackDocument

description:
Document plus lab results in; real ids out (D1).

The endpoint is transactional: the document and the whole
`procedure_order -> ... -> procedure_result` chain are written together,
so a partial write cannot leave results pointing at a document that was
never stored.

patient_uuid.description: FHIR Patient id. The endpoint resolves it to a pid; callers never send one.
patient_uuid.title: Patient Uuid

document_kind.description: Lab reports only. See the module docstring on D2.

extraction_id.description: The extraction run these results came from.
extraction_id.title: Extraction Id

extractor_version.description: Which extractor produced this run. Required, with no default: the ledger row records it, and a default would make every unstated run look like the same one.
extractor_version.title: Extractor Version
